_about: Dash 8-400 (DHC-8-402), from the Dash 8 Series 400 Airport Planning Manual (Bombardier, Dec 05/2014), Figure 2-2 Aircraft Dimensions (page index 26): side, plan and front views on one sheet; Figure 2-4 Maximum Ground Clearances (page index 28); Figure 2-11 passenger compartment cross section (page index 40: 106.0 in, 2.69 m, wide); Figures 2-18 to 2-22 door clearances (page index 49-58); Figure 2-26 sheet 3 emergency exits (page index 65). Black strokes (layers.py --mode strokes --color 0,0,0). The side view is drawn at the ground attitude, turned level (--rotate -1.26, from its crown and belly); the plan is drawn turned 31.92 degrees and 0.896 times the side's size, rendered to the side's scale (22.32) and turned level; the front view at 20.08 (its propellers 8.80 m apart, as printed). Pixels of those rasters, line centres. Scaled by the printed 31.04 m (101 ft 10 in) fuselage length, nose to tail cone. The side view draws 10 cabin windows ahead of the propeller and 5 behind the nacelle; the 15 the nacelle hides are placed on the same pitch (windowsAlso). Doors: the forward passenger (airstair) door and the aft passenger door on the left (Figures 2-18, 2-19: views on the L/H side), the aft baggage door on the left (Figure 2-22: a view inboard on the L/H side), the forward baggage door/Type I exit on the right (Figure 2-21: R/H side; drawn dashed in the left side view), the aft service door/Type I exit on the right (Figure 2-20: R/H side, at the aft passenger door's 21.88 m, its clear opening 1.48 m tall against the passenger door's 1.64 m: the passenger door's box, its top lowered by the difference). The propeller: 6 blades (Dowty R408, 1. Scope), its disc from the front view, its plane and the spinner from the side view.

sources.title: Bombardier, Dash 8 Series 400 Airport Planning Manual (Dec 05/2014): Figure 2-2 Aircraft Dimensions, Figure 2-4 Ground Clearances, Figure 2-11 Passenger Compartment Cross Section, Figures 2-18 to 2-22 Door Clearances, Figure 2-26 Emergency Exit Locations
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off Figure 2-2's side, plan and front views (tools/trace/dh8d/); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. The side view is drawn at the ground attitude and was turned level (1.26 degrees); the plan view is drawn turned and 0.896 times the side view's size and was rendered to its scale. The side view draws the fuselage 2.55 m tall, as the ground clearances put the crown 2.57 m over the belly (Figure 2-4) and the front view 2.59 m; the cross section prints its width (2.69 m), which the plan and front view draw. The nacelle hides 15 cabin windows in the side view: they're placed on the drawn windows' pitch. Doors' sides from each door's own clearance figure: the forward passenger (airstair) door, aft passenger door and aft baggage door on the left; the forward baggage door/Type I exit and the aft service door on the right (the service door at the passenger door's place, as its figure prints it, its opening 0.16 m shorter). Six-bladed propellers, 4.11 m across (Figure 2-26 sheet 3, Scope).

sources.note: Checked only: the cabin window row runs unbroken behind the propeller and nacelle, at about the drawn windows' pitch (0.50 m between the forward baggage door and the aft service door), as the windows placed behind the nacelle assume. No measurement taken from it.
